policy_title: Childcare Provider Funding Review and Career Strategy
stated: Ensure that all parents can access childcare that is flexible, affordable and fair by: Reviewing the rates paid to providers for free hours to ensure they cover the actual costs of delivering high-quality childcare and early years education. Developing a career strategy for nursery staff, including a training programme with the majority of those working with children aged two to four to have a relevant Early Years qualification or be working towards one. Including a specific emphasis on identifying and supporting children with special educational needs and disabilities in the new training programme for early years staff.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets early-years education quality through provider funding adequacy, staff qualification requirements, and SEND identification — all core drivers of school readiness and the attainment gap.

The explicit aim of 'affordable' childcare and reviewing provider funding rates bears materially on household childcare costs, which are a major budget pressure for working families with young children.

A dedicated career strategy with structured training and qualification pathways for nursery workers directly affects real wages, job quality, and career progression for workers in the early-years sector.

The stated goal of ensuring rates 'cover the actual costs' implies upward pressure on per-place public funding for free hours entitlements, representing a material increase in public expenditure that bears on fiscal sustainability.

membership_note: Four fundamentals: the policy's three components map cleanly onto O7 (education quality/SEND), O2 (childcare affordability for families), O4 (workforce career quality), and O12 (fiscal cost of correcting under-funded provider rates). Effects on O14 (attainment gap for SEND children) are real but subsumed within O7's attainment-gap indicator rather than constituting a separate inequality verdict.
